decisions.executionNote: Key is in left workspace; begin left elbow-up approach, keeping right clear. Will adapt grasp alignment from wrist view.
Continue smooth left approach and downward wrist rotation, leaving the other arm parked.
Advance toward the left-side key, gradually completing downward orientation; monitor joint continuity and wrist centering.
Bring left gripper above key shaft and match its slight in-plane angle. Remaining descent will be checked visually.
Replan with smaller increments after IK guard; center the key in the left wrist view and lower toward shaft grasp height.
Fine-center over the key shaft then close the left gripper; retention will be checked during a vertical lift.
Allow the left fingers to finish closing, then begin a small test lift without changing key orientation.
Lift the left-held key vertically above five centimeters while maintaining closure; check that it stays between the fingers.
Key appears retained but tilted; raise to handover height and rotate gradually toward the receiving right hand while inspecting retention.
Pause to inspect possible slippage; key no longer clearly lies between the left fingertips.
Key has slipped back onto the table. Reopen and approach the shaft again with a straighter top-down alignment, then recheck centering before closure.
Lower open fingers to a slightly deeper shaft grasp and align with the key's new angle. Inspect before closing.
Correct the remaining lateral shaft offset at grasp height and close without lifting yet, avoiding further downward table contact.
Hold the left wrist stationary while the fingers finish closing around the shaft; do not lift before visual confirmation.
The shaft is between the left fingers; keep the wrist still to let closure settle before lifting.
Make a slow 2 cm test lift with left closure maintained, watching for any key motion relative to the fingertips.
Continue a slow lift and slight retraction; the key is still visible between the fingers but its pitch is changing, so avoid rotation yet.
Keep closure and raise slowly toward transfer clearance; the key appears to pivot in the grasp, so verify whether it settles or slips before handover.
Key appears held near its toothed end and hangs downward. Raise and rotate left toward a central handover while beginning the right elbow-up receiving approach.
Key slipped during rotation. Stop both wrists and reopen left while it settles; next grasp will target the plain shaft nearer the bow rather than the teeth.
Approach the settled key's plain shaft near its bow, adapting to its diagonal orientation. Keep the receiving arm stationary and clear.
Finish aligning the wrist to the diagonal key and descend open to shaft-grasp height; inspect the plain shaft before closing.
Center the plain shaft between the fingers, slightly deepen the approach, and close at rest. Keep the toothed section clear of the pinch region.
Hold steady and maintain closed target while the left fingers finish approaching the centered shaft.
Lift vertically with the plain shaft pinched and left gripper held closed. Check that the key remains fixed relative to the fingers.
Key is now stable in the left pinch. Raise and retract toward handover clearance while the right arm approaches in elbow-up receiving orientation.
Continue the stable left-held key toward handover height, rotating its bow inward. Bring the right open fingers toward the bow without crossing the arms.
Hold the retained key at transfer height. Align the right fingers vertically around its inward-facing bow, approaching gradually from the right.
Complete the right receiving orientation while stopping short of the key bow. Left maintains the stable shaft grasp.
Replan after the IK guard with smaller right-arm increments, aligning its partially open fingers around the key bow while left stays closed.
Advance right fingers the final small distance onto the key bow and close. Left remains closed until right retention can be checked.
Keep both wrists stationary while the right fingers settle around the bow before releasing the left shaft grip.
Release the left shaft grip gradually while the right keeps the bow clamped; inspect the transfer before separating the wrists.
The bow appears retained by the right hand. Withdraw the open left hand outward while keeping right still to verify a clean handover.
Handover appears complete. Clear the left hand and raise the right-held key while beginning its upright insertion orientation, keeping well above the lock.
Continue raising and turning the right-held key toward vertical above the lock, preserving the elbow-up configuration and stable bow grasp.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller right wrist and height increments, continuing the retained key toward upright alignment.
Continue the right-held key's upright reorientation at safe height and move toward the visually estimated lock center. Left remains clear.
Continue gradual right wrist reorientation with the key retained by its bow; approach the lock laterally while keeping insertion clearance.
Move the right wrist over the lock center and continue toward a vertical key, keeping height unchanged until orientation is established.
Finish the upright wrist orientation over the lock without descending, then use the wrist image for precise slot alignment.
Use the wrist slot offset to translate the upright key toward the opening and lower cautiously, keeping the bow clamped.
Fine-adjust the key toward the visible slot center while lowering another 2 cm; maintain upright orientation and inspect before insertion.
The slot is now directly behind the upright shaft. Lower in small vertical increments, preserving alignment and watching for contact or slippage.
Possible rim contact: lift slightly before correcting the shaft toward the exposed slot edge. Avoid turning until the key seats.
Refine the remaining fore-aft and lateral slot offset with a small clearance lift; maintain an upright key before another insertion attempt.
Slot and shaft now appear centered. Insert vertically in small steps while keeping the right grasp closed and watching for seating rather than rim sliding.
Continue the centered vertical insertion by another small amount; the shaft remains upright and aligned in the wrist view.
Seat the key a little deeper, then begin a small controlled turn about its upright axis. Check the slot and retention before increasing rotation.
The key appears seated and retained during the initial turn. Continue rotating slowly about the upright axis without changing insertion depth.
Continue the seated key's gradual turn while holding depth constant; monitor the bow for slipping or tilting.
Complete more of the turn with a very small seating descent. The bow has shifted slightly, so use reduced increments and monitor upright retention.
Pause rotation to correct the visible shaft lean, shifting the wrist slightly toward the insertion axis with minimal upward relief while retaining the key.
Continue the last small portion of the turn with slight pivot compensation, preserving depth and monitoring the key's alignment in the slot.
Hold the turned key stationary to check whether it settles upright and remains seated; completion is not yet confirmed.
The key has shifted within the bow grasp rather than settling cleanly. Relieve depth slightly and ease the turn back to reduce binding before reseating.
Withdraw vertically to inspect the key's actual orientation and the asymmetric slot. The previous turn did not establish a clean upright seating.
Continue a short vertical inspection lift. The key may have remained at the slot rather than following the gripper; verify before changing orientation.
The key remains at the slot after the gripper withdrew. Reopen and realign above its bow for a controlled regrasp and upright correction.
Approach the exposed bow with open right fingers, using smaller downward and lateral adjustments before closing again.
Center the exposed bow between the right fingers and close at rest, keeping the key near its current slot engagement.
Hold the right wrist still while closure finishes around the centered bow; verify the regrasp before applying any turn.
